subject.title: fix(guarded-mkdir): allow in-root symlinked directory components

question: Should pinned writes support existing in-root symlinked parent directories consistently in both the Python helper and Node fallback, or should this PR remain intentionally fallback-only?
rationale: Allowing directory symlinks changes a filesystem boundary, while the current patch creates mode-dependent semantics; only maintainers can confirm whether helper parity or a deliberately narrower contract is intended.

options.title: Implement helper parity
options.body: Extend the Python helper with containment-preserving traversal and cover helper-enabled and helper-disabled writes with equivalent tests and live proof.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Limit and document the change as helper-disabled fallback compatibility, accepting that `auto` and `require` modes may continue rejecting the layout.

options.title: Pause symlink support
options.body: Keep unconditional parent-symlink rejection until a shared helper/fallback design can be reviewed as one security change.

recommendation.title: Implement helper parity
recommendation.body: Extend the Python helper with containment-preserving traversal and cover helper-enabled and helper-disabled writes with equivalent tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history ties this person to the original pinned-write security behavior and its current module structure.
